subject: RECORD DELIMITER clause (if not specified, method for determining length of variable-length records)
notes: A.1 item 151 — "RECORD DELIMITER clause (if not specified, method for determining length of variable-length records). This item is required. This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (12.4.5.11, RECORD DELIMITER clause, General rule 5)" (cite.py --check A.1 OK). The determination is filed in docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 and the compiler does what it says: a 4-byte little-endian length prefix per record for record sequential, relative and indexed files, the line delimiter for LINE SEQUENTIAL. It governs EVERY variable-length file this implementation writes, including one that does write a RECORD DELIMITER clause, because that clause is declined whole (§2 row 26, COBOL1778) — which is why the item is discharged rather than withdrawn: the clause's non-support makes GR5's method universal, not unreachable. Witnessed by golden file F4, the one file in it with no clause, whose 3- and 8-byte records read back at those lengths. retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/IO/RecordFraming.cs#PrefixLength (kb/Work PB2754 made RecordFraming.EncodeFrameHead the one encoder and RecordFraming.ReadFrame the one decoder of the documented 4-byte length prefix, as docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-151 now states; the Latin-1 char decoders, PrefixLength among them, were deleted, and WritePrefix had already been replaced by WriteFrameHead) retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/IO/RecordFraming.cs#WritePrefix (kb/Work PB2754 made RecordFraming.EncodeFrameHead the one encoder and RecordFraming.ReadFrame the one decoder of the documented 4-byte length prefix, as docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-151 now states; the Latin-1 char decoders, PrefixLength among them, were deleted, and WritePrefix had already been replaced by WriteFrameHead)
